title: Freyja: Not a Prize
subtitle: Love, war-magic, and the first pick of the dead — the goddess who refuses to be traded

learningObjectives.text: What powers does Freyja actually hold?
What does her refusal in the Thrym story show?

prose.author: Snorri Sturluson
prose.locator: Freyja and Folkvang in Gylfaginning; local text normalized characters 86916-87244
prose.excerpt: Freyja is the most famous of the goddesses. She has in heaven a dwelling which is called Folkvang, and when she rides to the battle, one half of the slain belong to her, and the other half to Odin. As is here said: Folkvang it is called, And there rules Freyja. For the seats in the hall Half of the slain She chooses each day;
prose.note: Verbatim Rasmus B. Anderson translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

poem.author: Anonymous Old Norse poets
poem.locator: Grímnismál, stanza 14; local text normalized characters 149488-149647
poem.excerpt: 14. The ninth is Folkvang, | where Freyja decrees Who shall have seats in the hall; The half of the dead | each day does she choose, And half does Othin have.
poem.note: Verbatim Henry Adams Bellows translation excerpt; whitespace normalized.

narrativeBlocks.title: The most-wanted goddess
narrativeBlocks.body: Freyja is the story every giant tries to win — Thrym asks for her as the hammer's price, and other giants try similarly. The myths' joke: everyone wants to 'marry Freyja' and nobody asks Freyja.

narrativeBlocks.title: The first chooser of the slain
narrativeBlocks.body: But she is not a love-object in her own right: she takes HALF the battle-dead to her hall Folkvangr, before Odin's Valhalla gets the rest. The honoured dead answer to her first.

narrativeBlocks.title: The teacher of seidr
narrativeBlocks.body: Freyja is mistress of seidr — Norse fate-magic — and the myths say she taught it to the gods themselves, including Odin. The goddess the giants want is also the witch who trained the Allfather.

narrativeBlocks.title: Her own grief
narrativeBlocks.body: Her husband Od wanders the world and she weeps golden tears searching for him — the myth keeps her as an agent with her own loss, not a pawn in giants' bargains.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why she refuses the trade
narrativeBlocks.body: When Thrym demands her, Freyja's fury shakes the hall and her necklace snaps — the outrage isn't just that she's asked, it's that the gods consider it. Her refusal is the myth's verdict on the bargaining.

quiz.prompt: What powers does Freyja hold beyond love?

choices.text: She takes half the battle-dead first and is mistress of seidr — the fate-magic she taught the gods

quiz.explanation: The 'love goddess' is also a war-power and the pantheon's magic-teacher.

quiz.prompt: How does Freyja react to being offered to Thrym?

choices.text: With fury that shakes the hall — the bargain is refused on her own terms, and Thor goes in disguise instead
She agrees reluctantly for the hammer's sake

quiz.explanation: Her refusal is decisive — the plan changes to costuming Thor.
